tagline: Muri makha, the way it's tossed at home and on every station platform.

golpo.title: Muri makha at home, jhaalmuri on the street
golpo.body: A big bowl tossed together for the evening cup of tea, for a rainy afternoon, or for an adda that won't end. On the street it's ঝালমুড়ি, spicy muri, shaken in a tin by vendors at stations, ferry ghats and on local trains, finished with a drizzle of raw mustard oil and handed over in a paper cone. Same dish, two names, and in both places it has to be eaten the minute it's made.

ingredients.item_en: Green chillies, chopped, plus ½ tsp green chilli paste

steps.action_bn: মুড়ি মুচমুচে কি না দেখে নাও।
steps.action_en: Check that the muri is properly crisp.
steps.maa_says: মিইয়ে যাওয়া মুড়িতে মুড়ি মাখা হয় না।

chemistry.title: Crisp is a state, Be like Muri
chemistry.explanation: Muri is rice starch puffed into a dry, brittle foam. Left open on a humid day it slowly drinks water from the air, and the brittle starch turns leathery, the way a biscuit tin left open in the monsoon goes soft. A little heat drives that water back out. The crunch matters more than you'd think: crisp, crackling food reads to us as fresh, and much of a crunch's sound is too high to hear but travels through the bones of your jaw, so you feel it as much as hear it.

steps.action_bn: আলু সেদ্ধ করে কিউব করে ঠান্ডা করো। পেঁয়াজ, লঙ্কা নাও, নারকেল সরু করে কাটো। টমেটোর ভেতরের শাঁস ফেলে শুধু বাইরের অংশটা কুচি করো।
steps.action_en: Boil, cube and cool the potato. Chop the onion, chillies, and cut the coconut into slivers. Scoop out the tomato's watery pulp and dice only the firm outer flesh.
steps.maa_says: টমেটোর শাঁস ফেলে দাও, নইলে মুড়ি নেতিয়ে যাবে।

chemistry.title: Every drop of water is the enemy
chemistry.explanation: In a curry, the tomato's jelly and seeds are where most of its flavour is. In muri makha they're simply water, and water is what kills the crunch, so out they go. Chop the onion just before you mix: cutting it starts the enzyme reactions that make its sharp, tear-jerking compounds, and they keep changing the longer it sits. The green chilli's heat lives mostly in the white pith that holds the seeds, not the seeds themselves, so leave the pith in for a properly jhal muri.

steps.action_bn: বড় বাটিতে মুড়ি, চানাচুর, আর বিটনুন মেশাও। তারপর মটর, লঙ্কা, আলু আর নারকেল দাও।
steps.action_en: In a big bowl, toss the muri with the chanachur and black salt. Then add the peas, chillies, potato and coconut.
steps.maa_says: শুকনো জিনিস আগে, ভেজা জিনিস একদম শেষে।

chemistry.title: Salt the dry part, never the wet
chemistry.explanation: Salt pulls water out of plant cells. Sprinkle it over chopped onion or tomato and they start weeping juice that goes straight into the muri, so the salt goes onto the dry ingredients first. Black salt adds that eggy, sulphurous note, from the traces of hydrogen sulphide and other sulphur salts it carries.

steps.action_bn: এবার লঙ্কা বাটা, আচারের তেল, কাঁচা সর্ষের তেল, পেঁয়াজ, টমেটো দিয়ে চটপট হাত চালিয়ে মেখে ফেলো।
steps.action_en: Now add the green chilli paste, pickle oil, raw mustard oil, onion and tomato, and toss quickly with your hands.
steps.maa_says: সর্ষের তেলের ঝাঁজ না থাকলে আবার ঝালমুড়ি!

chemistry.title: Raw mustard oil bites
chemistry.explanation: The sinus-clearing kick of raw mustard oil comes from allyl isothiocyanate, the molecule mustard makes to stop animals from eating it. Like the capsaicin in chilli, it sets off the same heat and pain sensors in your mouth and nose. It's volatile and fades when the oil is heated, which is why jhaalmuri uses the oil raw. A little sourness from the pickle oil and the tomato makes the chilli heat feel stronger, and the two hit the tongue slightly differently, so the muri tastes layered rather than flat.

molecules.name: Allyl isothiocyanate
molecules.note: The pungency of raw mustard oil.

molecules.name: Capsaicin
molecules.note: The heat of the green chillies.

trivia: ঝাল means spicy-hot and মুড়ি is puffed rice, so jhaalmuri is simply spicy puffed rice.

Bhelpuri is jhaalmuri's cousin from Mumbai's beaches. It's the same puffed rice with sev, potato and onion, but its flavour comes from sweet tamarind and green chutneys instead of mustard oil, so it's wetter, sweeter and tangier.
Aloor Chop, Chaa and Jhaalmuri is a classic trinity of taste!

quiz.question: Why does মা scoop the pulp out of the tomato?
options: The pulp is mostly water, and water turns the muri soggy
The pulp reacts with the mustard oil
It makes the tomato easier to chop
quiz.explain: In a curry the pulp is the best part. In jhaalmuri its water is the enemy of crunch.

quiz.question: Why is the mustard oil in jhaalmuri used raw, not heated?
options: Heated mustard oil turns bitter in muri
Raw oil keeps its pungent allyl isothiocyanate, which fades with heat
quiz.explain: The kick of mustard oil is volatile. Raw oil keeps it; heating drives it off.

further_reading: Krish Ashok, Masala Lab: The Science of Indian Cooking (Penguin, 2020): the chapters on spice, flavour and acids
Harold McGee, On Food and Cooking (2004): the chapters on seeds and grains, and on herbs and spices (why crisp things go soft, and mustard's pungency)

review.notes: Scaled to two servings. Science mostly from Masala Lab. Check: muri going leathery as it absorbs humid air, allyl isothiocyanate fading when mustard oil is heated, and muri being puffed in hot sand.
